items.justification: Automating an update mechanism versus protection of confidential training data and weights.
Authentication before network access versus maintaining an audit trail over models and datasets.
Per-device password uniqueness versus an audit log of model configuration changes.
Ease of applying an update versus security testing before release.
User guidance on checking secure setup versus logging changes to system prompts.
B names vulnerability remediation as a purpose of logging, and A is the remediation itself; the two make up one handling capability.
Machine-to-machine authentication method versus secure coding training.
Local operation during network loss versus secure coding training.
Alerting on detected tampering versus re-testing after a major system update.
Changing an authentication value versus internal channels for disseminating threat updates to staff.
Timely action on disclosed vulnerabilities versus justifying the use of poorly documented components.
Physical protection of debug ports versus advance notice of model updates.
Brute-force resistance versus threat modelling on configuration change.
Both are accessible disclosures to users, but of unrelated documents: support period versus component justification records.
Informing the user of a required update versus incident management and recovery planning.
Secure development processes versus technical measures supporting human oversight.
Both keep development-time capability out of reach in production, A by disabling debug interfaces, B by separating development environments.
Cryptographic strength of authentication versus involving Data Custodians in requirements discussions.
Management of critical security parameters versus security testing before release.
Prompt patching and support to affected users during an incident are different obligations under one response capability.
Password generation mechanism versus protection of confidential model weights.
Both govern how updates reach the user; A gives the user control over automation, B obliges proactive notification.
Secure development processes versus secure disposal on transfer of ownership.
Disabling debug interfaces versus confidentiality of training and test data.
Control over the automatic update mechanism versus general guidance on system use and configuration.
Recognizable model designation versus transparency about data use and storage.
Secure development processes versus disaster recovery planning.
Physical interface exposure versus documentation of design and maintenance plans.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus a threat modelling process naming data poisoning, model inversion and membership inference.
Setup guidance and communication of unresolved threats are different obligations that together equip the downstream party to manage risk.
Disabling unnecessary services versus accessible user guidance.
Physical protection of debug ports versus matching intended usage to data sensitivity.
Informing end users of a required update versus passing test findings to operators.
Both contain an incident and involve the right stakeholder, A automatically on the device, B as a documented support process.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus restorability of a known good state.
Secure boot verification versus publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy.
Both concern the update notification relationship with the user, A the user's control over it, B the obligation to notify and deliver.
Authentication before configuration change versus incident support for end users.
A secure development process depends on staff who know the current threats, which is what B mandates.
Setup guidance for consumers versus threat analysis and risk management by the developer.
